scopes.Noach: Selected Breslov teachings on Parshas Noach. Alternative readings are noted beside the affected passages.
scopes.Lech: Selected teachings and printed notes from pages 77–109, not the whole portion anthology or book. Wording, vocalization and citations remain uncertain where qualified beside the passages.

notes.readerText: “Offered up his life” means self-sacrifice for Israel; this clause does not say Moshe died in doing so.
The readings are uncertain: אֲמָרִית / אָמָרִית and עַלְוָון / עַלְוָן / עַלְוֹן.
The reading is uncertain: בְּעַיִּל / בְּעַיִּיל / בְּעַיִל.
בְּגָבְהָהּ / בְּגֹבְהָהּ / בְּגוֹבְהָהּ means “its height”; the spelling and vocalization are uncertain. The readings וַתָּנַח / וַתַּנַח and תִּשְׁרִי / תִשְׁרִי are also uncertain.
The first and second occurrences are each uncertain between ׳עַיִּל׳ / ׳עַיִּיל׳ / ׳עַיִל׳; neither occurrence settles the other.
The vocalizations are uncertain: הֵיצֵא / הֵיצֶא and בְּעַל / בַּעַל.
The vocalization of this occurrence is uncertain: עַיִּל / עַיִל.
The vocalization is uncertain: מְזֻמָּן / מְזֻמָן. The meaning is “ready.”
קש״ת is a mnemonic for three shofar sounds; their English names do not convey this Hebrew wordplay. The excerpt refers back to three points earlier in its source.
יַמְשִׁיךְ (“will draw down”) has no named subject: context may mean God acting through the righteous person, or the righteous person.
These occurrences have uncertain readings: בְּעַיִּל / בְּעַיִּיל / בְּעַיִל, אַפְתְּחַת / אַפְתְחַת and תַּרְעִין / תַרְעִין.
The printed citation is Laws of Shabbos, Halacha 4, item 69; the matching passage in the comparison text is Halacha 7, items 69–71.
“The aforementioned hidden kindness” refers to material earlier in the cited source, before this excerpt.
In “according to his power and will he sustains the world,” context points to the righteous person; vowel pointing alone does not settle the pronoun.
“Before Him” contextually means God. שֶׁנִּתַּן means “permission was given”; its passive clause does not name the giver, and pointing alone does not establish the divine referent.
The printed citation is Laws of Circumcision, Halacha 3, item 4; the matching comparison passage begins item 7.
“Flood/confusion” expresses the Hebrew wordplay מַבּוּל/בִּלְבּוּל. The parenthetical conversation is the source’s own report.
מָעֳמָד / מָעָמָד are alternatives: the ayin vowel is uncertain between hataf-kamatz and kamatz. The meaning is no standing place.
מַיִם׳ / מָיִם׳ are alternatives in the first depths-water quotation; the mem vowel is uncertain between patach and kamatz.
This occurrence of נִתְגַּלֶּה / נִתְגַּלָּה has an uncertain lamed vowel between segol and kamatz; the meaning is revelation.
The second occurrence is also uncertain between נִתְגַּלֶּה / נִתְגַּלָּה. This uncertainty does not apply to the earlier שנתגלה or the final-paragraph נתגלה.
No particular main teaching is identified for this printed note.
“[How could I]” is context supplied in English. וכ״ש שאתפלל על אחרים literally means “and all the more so that I should pray for others.”
ועבור לתחתונים על רצונך has no explicit word for offenses; “[by overlooking their offenses]” expresses the contextual sense.
למקומך reads “until you reach your place,” differing from the familiar maxim’s “his place.”
This note relates to the self-judgment teaching through its item 282 reference and subject matter; an explicit printed link is not established.
פ"מ (P.M.) is an unresolved acronym.
חִדּוּשׁ הָעוֹלָם means the world’s coming into being, not eternity; the passage is polemical.
אֲחָדִים means common words in the verse; חַדִּים means sharp words in its interpretation.
The initial-he vowel of הֻכְרַח is uncertain. The clause describes compulsion to come forth from Terach, without naming another acting subject.
כַּמָּה גִּלְגּוּלִין means many turnings—the divine circuitous means described by the events here—not necessarily multiple individual lifetimes.
היכלי התמורות and סטרא אחרא are technical chambers of exchanges and the Other Side.
מעש is a defective, unpointed noun amid the surrounding pointed text.
This note relates by its Likutay Torah on Iyov reference and subject matter to the captured-souls teaching; an explicit printed link is not established.
ע"י. ends the first nourishment clause without a following noun or pronoun. ‘[It]’ is supplied from the immediately repeated explanation that they are nourished through the soul.
ומצא has no expressed subject in this excerpt; “[he]” leaves the agent unspecified.
כי כיון (“for, since”) begins an irregular final clause that stops at במקום המטונף כזה (“in such a filthy place”).
Amatlai is a possible conventional rendering of unpointed אמתלאי; its vowels are uncertain.
Charan (חרן) is linked with wrath (חרון אף).
The lamed/yud vocalization of דְּאִתְגַּלְי' is uncertain in this occurrence.
Rabbainu means ‘our teacher’; this sentence does not give a personal name.
‘The above’ and ‘above’ refer to the argument within this text.
The singular ‘soul’ is followed by the masculine הוא (‘is’).
In note 56, “there” refers to the section 14 reference in the discussion of birth.
The wording shifts from plural ‘them’ to singular ‘his father’; the feminine form of ‘the essential’ refers to the soul.
‘[element]’ supplies an understood predicate in ‘the soul, which is the essential [element] in the person’; no corresponding noun appears in the Hebrew.
The singular pronouns follow a compound list. ‘He’ refers to the strengthening antagonist and ‘one’ to the person resisting him; no particular human antagonist is named.
נפשותינו משרשת has a plural noun, ‘our souls,’ with a singular feminine participle.
שמגדל concerns upbringing. שֶׁמְּגַדֵּל and שֶׁמְּגֻדָּל are possible readings; the vocalization is uncertain. No additional acting subject is identified.
The word is uncertain between שמרמזת and שמרומזת. “Alluding” leaves these alternatives open. The reference is to Yeshaya chapter 31.
ומה שירדה עליו שלותו and וכשם שהם היה קשה עליהם משא הדרך have difficult syntax in this quotation.
The outbreak term is uncertain between עֲפִישׁ and עֲפוּשׁ. The parallel wording עפוש suggests “pestilence,” but that meaning remains uncertain here.
The citation’s halacha numeral is uncertain between ז׳ (7) and ד׳ (4). The parallel teaching is in Halacha 7, which does not settle this citation. The item number is ע״ד (74).
The printed citation gives item 74; the electronic parallel is headed item 75. These are different numbering references.
The vocalization of this passage is uncertain.
The summary says ‘the suppressed evil’; the introduction and body say ‘the suppressed good.’ These are different readings.
This clause says ‘the altar is perfected’; the earlier introduction says ‘the imaginative faculty is perfected.’
This excerpt is shorter than the electronic parallel. Its vocalization is uncertain.
“Stopped up from above” is unclear here. The electronic Shabbos 7, item 8 passage differs from this quotation.
מגישים (“present at”) and the parenthesized מביטים (“look toward”) are alternative readings concerning the princes and his table.
מוהר״ר is an honorific; no personal name is given here.
The closing citation gives Rosh Chodesh, Halacha 6, item 45; the electronic parallel and note 65 give Halacha 7, item 45. The vocalization of this passage is uncertain.
The clause reads “sparks that fell from the depths of the shells.” The vocalization of this passage is uncertain.
The term bazak denotes a flashing appearance; the teaching connects it with broken earthenware and the fire between the shards.
מהר״א מששון is an abbreviated author designation; its full expansion is not established here.
The Hebrew parallels differ in wording and extent. The vocalization is uncertain, including זֻהֲמַת (“contamination”) in the Esther paragraph.
Sarah’s taking is linked here with the preceding discussion of Abraham’s trial.

The citation gives Tefillin, Halacha 6, item 27. The Chronicles reference differs between this excerpt’s chapter 36 and the electronic parallel. The vocalization is uncertain, including the separate זֻהֲמַת (“contamination”) occurrence in the other-side paragraph.
The backward reference after Moshe and Israel bringing Israel out of Pharaoh’s domain has no named target here.
Note 72 relates by context to the first teaching on page 99; an explicit source link is not established.

The quotations include difficult forms that differ from standard biblical wording; their reading is not settled by the standard wording. Notes 73 and 74 relate to this teaching by context, not an established explicit source link.
The Yiddish designation is uncertain: אָן דְעֲצִירְס and אָן זְעֲצִירְס are recorded alternatives, with the former also the provisional wording here.
The vocalization is uncertain between שִׁתִי and שִׁתִּי.
בְּתֹקֶף is an intensity noun, not “was repaired.” The clause concerns finding good within the intensity of the bad days’ prevailing.
This is a compiler’s aside within the surrounding discussion, not a separate main teaching or numbered note.
Note 73 relates by context to the second teaching beginning on page 99; an explicit source link is not established.
Note 74 relates by context to the second teaching beginning on page 99; an explicit source link is not established.
שֶׁהוּא וְשֹׁרֶשׁ literally reads ‘who is and root.’ The second ‘[is]’ supplies English syntax; the anomalous conjunction remains unresolved.

כעת חיה is interpreted here as “at this living time.” The two birth-noun occurrences have independently uncertain vocalizations. The printed Circumcision 4, item 16 citation differs from the Gairim 3 parallel; textual correspondence does not settle the citation.
The birth noun is הולדת. The vocalization הוֹלַדְת is uncertain; unpointed הולדת gives the consonants alone, not a settled alternative vocalization.
The later birth-noun occurrence הוֹלַדְתּוֹ has an independently uncertain vocalization, including the tav dagesh; the earlier occurrence does not settle it.
The citation is (הלכות מילה הלכה ד׳ אות ט״ז), Circumcision 4, item 16. The textual parallel is under Gairim, Halacha 3, a different reference; the citation’s authority remains unresolved.
The introduction and its Likutay Moharan II reference belong to the compiler, separately from the quoted body. The printed source reference is Partners in Land 5.
תמימות means wholehearted simplicity, in contrast to divination or forceful cleverness. The printed reference is Damages 5, item 16; the larger electronic parallel is item 15.

Note 75 relates by context to the concealed-Torah reference; an explicit source link is not established. The two occurrences discussed in the following qualifications have independently uncertain vocalizations.
The first occurrence is uncertain between בְּזַיִ״ן and בְּזַיִּ״ן.
The second occurrence is independently uncertain between הַזַּיִ״ן and הַזַּיִּ״ן.
Note 75 relates by context to the concealed-Torah reference; an explicit source link is not established.
No particular main teaching is identified for this note.
No particular main teaching is identified for this note.
והסתיר את עצמו כל המדריגות לפני הסט״א has no linking preposition before ‘all the levels.’ ‘[at]’ supplies a minimal English link; the intended construction remains uncertain.

The cited Zohar passage is 82a/b, not the electronic comparison’s 81b. The Moharan 62 quotation reads “beauty of the splendor and majesty of the glory”; the parallel differs in wording concerning speech and in excerpt extent.
No particular main teaching is identified for this note; proximity or subject matter does not establish an attachment.
